title: Operator Field Guide: Tiered Notification Maps and Status Cadence for Partial-Service Degradations
author: Maya Patel
body:
Summary / scope
This field guide defines a pragmatic, operator-friendly approach for handling partial-service degradations (instances where a subset of traffic, regions, or tenants experience elevated latency, increased error rate, or reduced throughput while the overall platform remains partially available). It covers detection thresholds, a tiered notification map, runbook actions for rapid stabilization, stakeholder communication templates, status-page cadence, game-day exercises, and post-incident review requirements.

Audience
- Primary: oncall engineers and SREs
- Secondary: platform/product incident leads, customer success (CS), and support engineers

When to use this document
Use this guide for incidents classified as:
- Severity 2 (partial-service degradation impacting >1% of requests but not full outage)
- Performance regressions affecting a cohort of tenants or a specific region/model variant
- Resource contention (e.g., KV cache thrash, node-level GPU stalls) leading to elevated tail latency

Key definitions
- Partial-service degradation: measurable, sustained deviation from SLOs for a subset of traffic or routes with no global outage.
- Primary oncall: first responder responsible for containment and triage for the service.
- Secondary oncall / escalation owner: second-line engineer who owns cross-service coordination and permissioned actions.
- Incident owner: person assigned to drive communications and post-incident actions.

Detection thresholds (examples we monitor)
1) Latency: 95th percentile request latency for text-generation endpoints > 500ms for 3 consecutive one-minute windows and 95th latency increase > 2x relative to baseline.
2) Error rate: request error ratio > 1.0% for 2 minutes or > 0.5% sustained for 15 minutes.
3) Throughput: tail throughput drops > 20% for a region for 10 minutes while other regions normal.
4) Capacity signals: queued-requests > 2000 on a serving pool or KV cache eviction rate > 30% sustained for 5 minutes.

Severity classification (applicable to partial degradations)
- Sev-1: Global outage or customer-impacting catastrophic failure (use outage playbooks).
- Sev-2: Partial-service degradation with high customer impact across multiple tenants or regions.
- Sev-3: Localized degradation (single tenant or feature flagged traffic) with limited impact.

Tiered notification map (decision table)
- Criteria: use the first row that matches. Notification delays are *wall-clock* after detection.

1) Criteria: Latency 95th > 2x baseline AND error rate > 0.5% for 10m -> Severity Sev-2
   - Notify: Primary oncall (pager immediate), Secondary oncall (15m), Service Owner (15m), CS Triage (30m)
   - Escalate to on-call manager if unresolved after 60m

2) Criteria: KV cache eviction > 30% for 5m OR queued-requests > 2000 -> Severity Sev-2
   - Notify: Primary oncall (pager immediate), SRE/Infra runbook group channel (Slack @here 5m), Secondary oncall (20m), Product PM (30m)

3) Criteria: Single-tenant errors > 5% for 10m -> Severity Sev-3
   - Notify: Primary oncall (primary alert), Tenant owner (email/CS), Secondary only if unresolved after 2 hours

Notification channels and templates
- PagerDuty: use the service escalation policy for the affected service. Short summary + link to evidence (alerts dashboard).
- Slack: post to #prod-ops-bridge with header: [INCIDENT | Sev-2] <service> partial degradation (region/tenant). Include one-line impact, top 3 signals, first stabilization step taken, and link to live metrics.
- Email/CS: use the "Customer triage" template below for impacted tenants identified in the first 30 minutes.

Customer triage template (CS/Support)
Subject: "Redwood Inference — Service degradation observed for <tenant-name> — <short impact>"
Body:
Hi <Customer Name>,

We are investigating an elevated latency and intermittent errors affecting <service/route>. Impact: <e.g., 8% of requests from your account in us-west experienced 95p latency > 800ms between 14:05–14:32 UTC>.
What we are doing: our oncall team has executed containment steps and is working on root-cause triage. We will provide an update in 30 minutes.
If you are experiencing blocking issues, reply to this message or open a ticket and mention incident id: <INC-YYYYMMDD-####>.

Timeline & Cadence for status updates
- T+0 (detection): Pager alert and Slack bridge created. Short triage note posted.
- T+15: initial Slack + internal status note (private to internal teams).
- T+30: Customer-facing update if tenant-impacting (use Customer triage template).
- Every 60 minutes: status update for ongoing incidents.
- At stabilization (traffic within SLOs for 15 minutes): publish recovery note + post-incident owner assignment.
- Within 72 hours: postmortem draft created.

Runbook actions (quick checklist for primary oncall)
1) Acknowledge alert and mark start time in incident tracker (INC-YYYYMMDD-####).
2) Create Slack bridge: #ops-bridge-<incident-id> and invite Secondary, Infra, Product PM, CS lead.
3) Attach evidence: link to traces, error logs, and capacity dashboards.
4) Attempt safe containment (examples):
   - For KV cache thrash: disable non-essential writes, reduce write amplification (feature-flag), scale read pool by +1 NPU instance if autoscaling available.
   - For model stall / high decode latency: fallback to a lower-latency model variant with the same API surface (use routing policy: fallback:model:a1-low-latency).
   - For noisy neighbors: evict suspect tasks from the serving pool, cordon the node.
5) If containment requires a restart or rollout, coordinate with Secondary and apply canary for affected fleet slice (5–10% traffic).
6) Monitor outcomes for 15 minutes; if the metric direction improves, expand the fix and begin recovery sequence.

Escalation timing and ownership
- Primary should escalate to Secondary after 30 minutes if the incident is not contained OR if any of the following apply: ongoing customer-visible degradation, cross-team coordination required, or required permissioned action (e.g., manual database schema change).
- Secondary becomes Incident Owner by convention when they are paged in. The Incident Owner is responsible for high level communications and the postmortem.

Status page and public messaging strategy
- Status states: Operational, Degraded, Partial Outage, Major Outage. For partial-service degradations use "Degraded" or "Partial Outage" depending on affected fraction.
- Public message template for status page (short):
   Title: "Partial degradation in <region/service> — <short summary>"
   Body: "We are seeing elevated latency affecting a subset of requests to <service> in <region>. Our engineers are investigating. Impact: <estimated % of requests>. Next update: in 60 minutes."
- Internal description should include the incident id, primary mitigations attempted, and the route to the closest postmortem draft.

Game-day exercise (simulation blueprint)
- Objective: validate operator decision-making for a KV cache thrash causing 95p latency spikes in us-east and rolling through the serving pool.
- Participants: 1 primary oncall, 1 secondary oncall, 2 infra engineers, 1 product PM, 1 CS observer.
- Timeline (3 hours):
   - 0–15m: detection via synthetic alerts.
   - 15–30m: triage and containment (disable non-essential writes).
   - 30–60m: simulate a failed canary and require manual routing fallback.
   - 60–120m: restore capacity and verify recovery.
   - 120–180m: retro and blameless postmortem (complete template).
- Success criteria: containment in <45m, recovery in <90m, retrospective and action items created.

Evidence capture checklist (must be preserved)
- Timestamped metric snapshots (95p latency, error rates, queued requests)
- Representative traces (one successful, one failing)
- Node-level logs for implicated hosts
- PagerDuty timeline and Slack bridge transcript (export)
- Any configuration changes or rollouts applied

Post-incident review template (minimal required fields)
- Incident id: INC-YYYYMMDD-####
- Summary: one-paragraph impact statement
- Detection time / Recovery time / Time to mitigate
- Root cause: concise statement
- Contributing factors (3–5 bullets)
- Corrective actions (owner + due date)
- Preventative actions and monitoring changes (owner + due date)
- Severity justification and customer impact assessment

Operational checklists (quick reference)
- If 95p latency increases by >2x: create Slack bridge, page Secondary, consider immediate fallback route.
- If queued requests >2000: reduce ingestion rate, enable backpressure, and scale serving pool.
- If single-tenant >5% errors: contact CS for customer-specific mitigation and track separately.

Quick CLI examples
- Create bridge channel (using internal tooling):
  curl -X POST \
    -H \"Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN\" \
    -H \"Content-Type: application/json\" \
    -d '{"name":"ops-bridge-INC-20260215-001","topic":"Partial degradation - kv cache"}' \
    https://internal-api.redwoodops/api/v1/bridges

- Trigger a status page update (example):
  curl -X POST \
    -H \"Authorization: Bearer $STATUS_TOKEN\" \
    -H \"Content-Type: application/json\" \
    -d '{"state":"degraded","title":"Partial degradation in us-east","body":"Elevated latency for a subset of requests (estimated 6% impact). Next update in 60 minutes."}' \
    https://status.redwood.ai/api/v1/incidents

Ownership and oncall rotation guidance
- Rotation model: 2-week primary rotation with 1-week secondary rotation. Primary is expected to handle weekday incidents during shift; secondary supports escalations and major permissioned changes.
- Handover checklist for shifts:
   - Review active incidents and running bridges
   - Confirm alert fidelity and muted alerts are documented
   - Confirm runbook access and keys/certificates are valid
- Time expectations: primary must acknowledge high-severity pages within 2 minutes and post the first triage note in Slack within 10 minutes.

Metrics and SLO tie-ins
- Where possible, annotate incidents with which SLO(s) were impacted (latency_p95, request_error_rate, kv_cache_eviction_rate). This helps prioritize RCA and customer comms.

Appendix: example postmortem first paragraph (blameless)
On 2026-02-15 at 14:03 UTC we observed elevated 95th percentile latency for the text-generation service concentrated in the us-east region. Approximately 6% of requests experienced latency above our SLO for a 32-minute window. The oncall team executed containment by scaling the read pool and enabling a model fallback; final recovery occurred at 14:35 UTC. Root cause analysis identified a combination of a misconfigured cache eviction policy and a regression in autoscaler heuristics.

- Model fallback routing: /runbooks/model-fallbacks

Contact for questions
If anything in this guide is unclear or you want to propose changes, ping the eng-sre documentation owner: Maya Patel (maya@redwood.ai) or open a PR against the playbook repo.
